report:
Case sensitive error when deleting records

Hi Debezium team,
We use Oracle Source Connector and JDBC sink connector debezium 2.6 to capture change from Oracle Database 19c to PGDB 15.16.
We got this error when sink deleted events to PostgreSQL eventhough insert or update events are successful. (With or without tombstones).
	Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
	at io.debezium.connector.jdbc.dialect.postgres.PostgresDatabaseDialect.getQueryBindingWithValueCast(PostgresDatabaseDialect.java:123)
	at io.debezium.connector.jdbc.type.AbstractType.getQueryBinding(AbstractType.java:37)
Please help us resolve this issue.

evidence.quote: Please implement a ColumnNamingStrategy... would simply lower case the field names... guarantee that the JDBC sink code will find and use the columns correctly." Reporter: "I have fixed the error of not being able to delete.

notes: NPE in PostgresDatabaseDialect.getQueryBindingWithValueCast on deletes looks like a bug, but it stems from upper-case source field names vs pre-created lower-case target columns; fixed via column.naming.strategy.

reviews.fix: Implement a ColumnNamingStrategy that lowercases field names and set it via column.naming.strategy on the JDBC sink.
reviews.evidence: Oanh Nguyen: "Thank you for your guidance, I have fixed the error of not being able to delete." after Chris: "Please implement a ColumnNamingStrategy and specify... `column.naming.strategy`"
reviews.boundary: B vs D: the NPE on deletes looks like a defect, but it was resolved by configuring naming for case-sensitive identifiers without a code change, so B

reviews.fix: Configured a custom ColumnNamingStrategy (column.naming.strategy) in the JDBC sink to lower-case field names so the sink finds the pre-created PostgreSQL columns.
reviews.evidence: Chris Cranford: "Please implement a ColumnNamingStrategy and specify the fully qualified class name using `column.naming.strategy`"; Oanh Nguyen: "I have fixed the error of not being able to delete."
reviews.boundary: B vs D: the NPE looked like a defect, but the resolution was an application setting (naming strategy) matching the user's case-sensitive schema, so B.
